(2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: StreamableHTTP client hangs/fails silently when SSE reconnection permanently fails (MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS exceeded in _handle_reconnection) — the waiting caller previously received no signal that the stream was dead. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: StreamableHTTP client hangs/fails silently when SSE reconnection permanently fails (MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS exceeded in _handle_reconnection) — the waiting caller previously received no signal that the stream was dead. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2395's diff is a complete, self-contained fix directly at the bug site in _handle_reconnection: it builds a JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer so the specific pending request is unblocked with a normal JSON-RPC error response, consistent with the existing ErrorData/JSONRPCError/INTERNAL_ERROR pattern already used elsewhere in this file. It also upgrades the previously swallowed pragma:no-cover debug log to a warning. 3098 addresses the same symptom via a different mechanism — a generic _unwrap_exception helper that pulls a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup so it propagates to the caller as a raised exception rather than a protocol-level error message — and its diff also includes an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`), giving it more surface area and higher risk of merge conflicts against 2395's narrower, targeted change.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parses the WWW-Authenticate header with logic that doesn't properly respect quoted auth-param values, causing substring/param matches to bleed across comma-separated tokens (e.g. matching inside quoted strings or across unrelated params) instead of matching complete, correctly-delimited auth-params. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parses the WWW-Authenticate header with logic that doesn't properly respect quoted auth-param values, causing substring/param matches to bleed across comma-separated tokens (e.g. matching inside quoted strings or across unrelated params) instead of matching complete, correctly-delimited auth-params. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting state machine at the same location in utils.py, but #3012's _iter_www_auth_params treats everything after the first space as one flat list of params for a single scheme, so it doesn't scope extraction to a specific challenge when a header contains multiple schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer error=...'). #3041 adds _split_www_authenticate_segments plus _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly walks per-scheme segments and only collects auth-params belonging to the Bearer challenge, so it correctly handles multi-challenge WWW-Authenticate headers that #3012's approach would misparse.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly runs json.loads() on string parameter values whose annotation is a union containing str (most commonly `str | None`), corrupting valid strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a plain str/Optional[str] argument). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly runs json.loads() on string parameter values whose annotation is a union containing str (most commonly `str | None`), corrupting valid strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a plain str/Optional[str] argument). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056's _is_optional_str only skips pre-parsing when the union is exactly str/None (after unwrapping Annotated), so behavior for other simple-type unions like str|int or str|bool is left unchanged (a JSON-looking string can still be coerced to int/bool as before). It also explicitly unwraps Annotated via _unwrap_annotated, so the common FastMCP pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` is correctly detected. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead treats any union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} as skippable, which silently changes existing JSON-coercion behavior for str|int/str|bool/str|float params beyond the reported bug, and it does not unwrap Annotated, so it fails to fix the very Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None case that is idiomatic for described optional string parameters.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart (cold start), OAuthContext.oauth_metadata is empty, so _refresh_token has no discovered authorization-server/token endpoint to use, causing refresh to fail or require full rediscovery. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart (cold start), OAuthContext.oauth_metadata is empty, so _refresh_token has no discovered authorization-server/token endpoint to use, causing refresh to fail or require full rediscovery. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3263 fixes the cold-start refresh gap for every caller immediately by performing AS metadata discovery before the refresh attempt (tracked via a new eager_discovery_attempted flag) and adds an issuer-binding check on the rediscovered metadata. 2492 instead adds optional get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata methods to the TokenStorage protocol with no-op defaults — it only fixes the problem for TokenStorage implementations that adopt the new methods, leaving default/unmodified storage backends with the original bug, and it has no equivalent issuer-binding validation on the persisted metadata.

clusters.pick_reason: 2395's diff is a complete, self-contained fix directly at the bug site in _handle_reconnection: it builds a JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer so the specific pending request is unblocked with a normal JSON-RPC error response, consistent with the existing ErrorData/JSONRPCError/INTERNAL_ERROR pattern already used elsewhere in this file. It also upgrades the previously swallowed pragma:no-cover debug log to a warning. 3098 addresses the same symptom via a different mechanism — a generic _unwrap_exception helper that pulls a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup so it propagates to the caller as a raised exception rather than a protocol-level error message — and its diff also includes an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`), giving it more surface area and higher risk of merge conflicts against 2395's narrower, targeted change.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962 guards the whole mismatch check with `has_tool_results`, so when no tool_result blocks are present at all, validation is skipped and no error is raised — matching SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but places no requirement that tool_use be followed by tool_result; it also adds a regression test tied to issue #2960. #3053 touches the same condition but keeps the raise, just replacing the message ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') — this is the opposite behavior (still an error in the exact case #2962's spec citation says is valid), so it isn't a compatible/equivalent fix and would reintroduce the failure #2962's regression test checks for.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting state machine at the same location in utils.py, but #3012's _iter_www_auth_params treats everything after the first space as one flat list of params for a single scheme, so it doesn't scope extraction to a specific challenge when a header contains multiple schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer error=...'). #3041 adds _split_www_authenticate_segments plus _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly walks per-scheme segments and only collects auth-params belonging to the Bearer challenge, so it correctly handles multi-challenge WWW-Authenticate headers that #3012's approach would misparse.
